best_for: Indie and hobby game developers building 2D tile-based levels who want a free editor whose maps load in Godot, Unity, Phaser and many other engines.
description:
Tiled is a free, open source level editor for 2D games, made by Thorbjørn Lindeijer and many other contributors since 2008. At the time of reading, over 200 sponsors gave about $3,600 a month, which pays for him to work on Tiled two days a week. Shovel Knight, Axiom Verge, Carrion and Coromon all used it to build their levels.

Automapping places the right tiles for you by following rules you set. On object layers you can mark up a level with rectangles, ellipses and polygons, and place, resize and rotate tiles freely. Object templates save you from setting up the same object again and again. You can group several maps into a world, jump to any file in a project, and set your own keyboard shortcuts.

points.title: Free, paid for by sponsors
points.text: Tiled is free and open source under the GPL. Development runs on donations and sponsors, with no paid edition.

points.title: Square, isometric and hex maps
points.text: It handles orthogonal, isometric and hexagonal maps, plus infinite maps that grow as you paint. Maps can mix several tilesets and have as many layers as you need.

points.title: Your engine probably reads it
points.text: Tiled saves its own TMX format and exports to JSON, Lua, GameMaker, Defold, Godot 4 scenes and more. The docs list loaders for Unity, Phaser, LibGDX, Bevy and others.

points.title: Scriptable in JavaScript
points.text: You can add custom file formats, new tools and actions in JavaScript, which helps when your engine needs a format Tiled does not ship.

points.title: It edits maps, it does not run them
points.text: Tiled is a level editor only. Collision, game logic and rendering stay in your engine or in a loader you pick.

points.title: Linux Flatpak by the author
points.text: The Flathub build is verified for Thorbjørn Lindeijer through the mapeditor.org website, in x64 and Arm64. The Windows installers are machine-wide in 32-bit and 64-bit; the Mac build is one universal .zip.

points.title: Older versions: Windows only
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 23 versions. macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
